python_best_practices.description: More Pythonic way to create lists
python_best_practices.explanation: List comprehensions are faster and more readable than loops for simple transformations

python_best_practices.good:
with open('file.txt') as f:
    data = f.read()
python_best_practices.explanation: Context managers ensure files are closed even if errors occur
Generators don't store all values in memory, they produce them on demand

python_best_practices.description: Static type checking for better code clarity
python_best_practices.bad:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b
python_best_practices.good:
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a + b
python_best_practices.explanation: Type hints help IDEs detect errors and make code self-documenting
Catch specific exceptions and handle them appropriately, don't silently ignore errors

performance_tips.why: String concatenation creates new objects each time. join() is O(n), += is O(n squared)

performance_tips.issue: Multiple lookups instead of using get()
performance_tips.why: get() performs one lookup instead of two
Set lookup is constant time, list lookup is linear

security_issues.vulnerable: query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}"
security_issues.why: Parameterized queries prevent SQL injection attacks

security_issues.danger: Storing API keys in source code
security_issues.why: Use environment variables to keep secrets out of version control
pickle can execute arbitrary code. Use json for untrusted data

common_mistakes.problem: Default list is created once and shared across calls

common_mistakes.code: funcs = [lambda x: i*x for i in range(3)]
common_mistakes.problem: All lambdas reference the same 'i' variable
common_mistakes.solution: funcs = [lambda x, i=i: i*x for i in range(3)]

common_mistakes.code: # Code at module level that runs on import
common_mistakes.problem: Code runs when module is imported, not just when executed

readability_patterns.why: Code is read more often than written

readability_patterns.without:
def calculate(a, b):
    return a + b
readability_patterns.why: Docstrings help users understand function purpose

readability_patterns.long: result = some_function(arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5) if condition else alternative
readability_patterns.why: Long lines are hard to read and debug
